text:
Please help me write our investor update for the half year. We make sensors that sit inside beehives and tell commercial beekeepers when a colony is weak, so they can treat it before it dies. We're raising a $600,000 bridge round and I want our current investors in it.

Where we are:
- We have 31 paying beekeepers. A year ago we had 12.
- Each sensor costs us $38 to make and we sell it for $55, plus $4 a month per hive for the app.
- Revenue for the last six months was $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, before pollination season.
- Our biggest customer runs 4,000 hives and lost 18% of his colonies over the winter, against 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of it, but he also changed his mite treatment.
- We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 left.
- A large farm equipment company launched a similar sensor in May at $45.

I want the update to say we'll be profitable next year. Keep it under 600 words.

Before I draft, a few questions. Your current investors will check the numbers, so the answers decide how the piece makes its case.

1. **What does "profitable next year" rest on?** How many hives are paying the $4/month app fee right now, what sensor sales do you expect next spring, and are you planning any cost cuts? At $95k a month in spending, investors will want to see roughly how revenue catches up. Without those figures, the claim will read as hope.
2. **What does the $600k get you to?** Profitability, or a priced round? What are the terms (SAFE or note, cap, discount), when do you want it closed, and has anyone committed yet? This matters because $340k at $95k a month lasts about 3.5 months. That's roughly early March, just as your strong season starts.
3. **How do you answer the $45 competitor?** Have you lost any customers or deals to them since May, or kept any who looked at them? What do you have that they don't?
4. **Can I name or quote your biggest customer?** Is he renewing or adding hives? I'll describe his winter results the way you did: sensors plus a change in mite treatment.
5. **Is anything changing on cost?** For example, the $38 sensor cost dropping at higher volume, or changes to headcount.

If you don't know an answer, just say so. I'll write around it without guessing.

1. I don't know the exact number of hives on the app fee or what spring sensor sales will be. On costs, we can get spending down to $75k a month by February by not filling two open roles. Honestly, I can't promise profit next year. If the numbers don't support it, say what they do support.

2. Not sure exactly what it gets us to. It's a convertible note with a 20% discount and a $6M cap, closing December 15. One angel has already committed $250k.

3. I don't know if we've lost any deals to them. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test their sensor. Theirs only measures temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight.

4. I don't know if I can name or quote him, or whether he's renewing or adding hives.

5. Just the spending cut to $75k a month by February. I don't know about the sensor cost dropping.

I've written the update below. I couldn't support "profitable next year" with your numbers, so the update says what they do support. Revenue has averaged about $35k a month. Even after you cut spending to $75k a month, revenue would need to roughly double to break even. What the numbers do show is that the bridge carries you through next spring's selling season, which will show whether you can get there.

**Subject: Half-year update and bridge round**

Hi all,

Here's where we stand at the half year, and what I'm asking of you.

**The short version**

We have 31 paying beekeepers, up from 12 a year ago. Revenue for the last six months was $212,000. We have $340,000 in the bank and spend about $95,000 a month. We're raising a $600,000 bridge on a convertible note to carry us through next spring's pollination season. An angel investor has already committed $250,000. I'd like you in this round.

**What went well**

- **Customers:** 12 to 31 in a year.
- **Revenue:** $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, when beekeepers get colonies ready for pollination. That's when our customers buy, and it shapes our whole year.
- **Margins:** Each sensor costs us $38 to make and sells for $55. Customers also pay $4 per hive per month for the app. We make money on every unit we sell.
- **Results:** Our largest customer runs 4,000 hives. He lost 18% of his colonies this winter, compared with 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of that. He also changed his mite treatment, so we can't take credit for the whole improvement. But it's the result we built this product to deliver.

**What's harder**

- **Competition.** In May, a large farm equipment company launched a similar sensor at $45. Theirs measures only temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test their sensor. We don't yet know whether we've lost any deals to them. I'll report what we learn from those tests.
- **Cash.** At today's spending, our $340,000 lasts until about March. That's just as our selling season starts. The bridge is meant to solve this.

**Will we be profitable next year?**

I can't promise that, and I won't tell you something the numbers don't support. Over the last six months, revenue averaged about $35,000 a month against $95,000 in spending.

Here is what the numbers do support:

- **Lower spending.** We're bringing spending down to $75,000 a month by February by not filling two open roles.
- **Runway through next season.** With the bridge closed, we have cash into autumn 2027 before counting any new revenue. That covers all of next spring's buying season, with room to spare.
- **A real test.** Next spring will show how many existing customers add hives, how many new ones we win against a cheaper competitor, and how close app revenue gets us to covering our costs. I'll share those numbers with you after the season, and they'll tell us honestly how far we are from profitability.

**The round**

- $600,000 convertible note
- 20% discount, $6M cap
- Closes December 15
- $250,000 committed; $350,000 still open

If you'd like to take part, reply by [date] with the amount and I'll send the documents. I'm happy to get on a call to go through the numbers.

Thank you for backing us.

[Your name]
</final_document>

A few notes:

- **Runway math:** I assumed $95k a month through January and $75k from February. With $940k after the bridge, that lasts until about November 2027, counting no new revenue. Without the bridge, the money runs out around March.
- **Your largest customer:** He's described but not named, because you weren't sure you could name him. If he agrees to be quoted, or is adding hives, that would be the strongest line in the update.
- **Missing figure:** Once you have the number of hives paying the app fee, add it. It's the figure investors will look at first when judging whether you can become profitable.
- **Placeholders:** Fill in the reply-by date and your name. The update is about 480 words.
